The Topic

This discussion does not include whether influence is good or bad, but simply how you feel about Reddit-specific influences throughout WhoaVerse. For example, some subverses are arguably clones from their counterparts on Reddit: Conspiracy, TIL, bestof, IAMA, etc. Some even have the same rules and focus.

This topic has been floating in my head for a while and, since it's been quiet lately, I wanted to start a discussion to hear everyone's thoughts.

To start the discussion off strong, here are some ideas/subtopics:

  • Does it make WhoaVerse look bad if some subverses and terms are identical to those of Reddit?

  • Should it or shouldn't it be considerable to eventually form unique terms and subverses to differentiate WhoaVerse from Reddit?

  • Should it matter that WhoaVerse is considered a clone?

The discussion as a whole is not limited to the preceding points. Feel free to discuss anything within the boundaries of the question in the title:

What do you think about Reddit-specific influences throughout WhoaVerse?

Thank you for your time and contribution in this discussion. :-)

My Opinion

I, personally, think that it is detrimental to the reputation of WhoaVerse that many of the things throughout our community are directly influenced by Reddit. It reinforces, at least for outsiders, the idea that this site is a 'clone'.

I care about how WhoaVerse is thought of, at least regarding claims of it to be a 'clone'. Because of this, I think it should be considered greatly how we can differentiate ourselves from Reddit's community.

I think that, instead of transferring elements of Reddit — sometimes even entire subreddits — to the community here, we should consider evolving it as an individual entity. There is a lot of gray area to this proposition, however, because the Internet is all about influences and hyperlinks.
What do you think about Reddit-specific influences throughout WhoaVerse?

Does it make WhoaVerse look bad if some subverses and terms are identical to those of Reddit?

Does it make McDonalds look bad if some food offerings (burgers, fries, soda) and sizing (Supersize/Kingsize) are superficially the same as Burger King (or vice versa)?

Sure they'll call them different things, but when it gets right down to it, Supersize = Kingsize just like Karma = Internet Points. Where I live, there's a playland at McDonalds and a Play Place at Burger King (I may have the phrasing wrong, but I hope you get my point -- they're both fast food burger joints with a place to entertain the kids).

So the question is: how does Burger King thrive in the presence of McDonalds (or vice versa)? They create their own spin on content. It's not that both sites have a place called TIL, but TIL needs to be different. Not everything has to be different (you can get a plain cheeseburger with ketchup, fries, and a small coke at both places - but there are unique offerings at both).

Reddit loves to bash other online media (9gag, Twitter, Tumbler, etc.). Perhaps Whoaverse could be the place that accepts that some people still visit ebaumsworld and Whoaverse won't give people grief over it. That would actually be refreshing.

Should it or shouldn't it be considerable to eventually form unique terms and subverses to differentiate WhoaVerse from Reddit?

Yes, but not exclusively. See my above answer.

Should it matter that WhoaVerse is considered a clone?

No, because with time and membership, whoaverse will be different. Forget the whole fast food ideas. Look at 4chan and 7chan (and other chans) - they are the same - but are unique. I don't see one shutting down because the other exists.

imgur hasn't shut down Flickr. Google hasn't shutdown Yahoo, Bing, or DuckDuckGo. Gmail hasn't stopped umpteen hundreds of other email services. It's OK to be a clone as long as people can see differences. These differences are submissions. As the number of posters vary, so will the contents. And this is a aggregator of content.

Right now, Whoaverse is relatively small. Reddit has Subreddits with more people subscribed than Whoaverse has seen visitors. It's still growing.

There are going to be Redditesque similarities for a while until Whoaverse really gets its mojo going. But it's small and there's still time.

Does it make McDonalds look bad if some food offerings (burgers, fries, soda) and sizing (Supersize/Kingsize) are superficially the same as Burger King (or vice versa)?

Analogies cannot be applied here since this type of concept is judged on a case by case basis. Fast food restaurants specialized in burgers, like McDonald's and Burger King, are limited in what they sell so they do not stray too much in what their customers expect. All of their food tastes differently, they have different recipes, and they call them different things.

Some subverses, on the other hand, are called the same thing, have the same general rules and focus, and have the same community within.

We are not talking about theoreticals. There are comments on Reddit talking about how WhoaVerse is a clone and, as I have suggested in the post, they are partially right. Whether or not they assume correctly is not really my concern; it is the point that WhoaVerse looks bad.

Reddit loves to bash other online media (9gag, Twitter, Tumbler, etc.). Perhaps Whoaverse could be the place that accepts that some people still visit ebaumsworld and Whoaverse won't give people grief over it. That would actually be refreshing.

This is one of the disappointments I have with Reddit. Sometimes circlejerking (if I used that term correctly) spread throughout subreddits and it annoyed me greatly. Especially when, according to a few posts I have seen, WhoaVerse has unreasonably been caught in the fire.

This would be a necessity in an ideal community for me and, so far, the community here has demonstrated that it is capable of honoring it.

There are going to be Redditesque similarities for a while until Whoaverse really gets it mojo going. But it's small and there's still time.

I agree. I just feel that it may need to be concentrated a bit to ensure that there is enough differential for WhoaVerse to gain respect from much of the Reddit community (even though I believe WhoaVerse is still unknown to most). These points do not actually reflect on my opinions; they were just sample talking points so anyone could easily join the discussion and know what is being discussed.

Thank you for your thoughts.
